environment.concurrentWorkloads: No build or other benchmark started by this harness; other host activity is not controlled.

webView.userAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/155.0.0.0 Safari/537.36 Edg/155.0.0.0

method.workload: Production sync pull(config) returning one complete demo config with a synthetic ASCII field of 1 KiB, 64 KiB or 1 MiB. No echo service or transport API replacement.
method.scope: WebView immediately before production store.send to the first production configStore reference update. Includes request dispatch, selected carrier, Python cached snapshot deepcopy, JSON, authenticated encryption for WebSocket, Rust/WebView bridge where applicable and synchronous Store subscribers before this observer. Excludes CDP, configuration writes, connection restart, content validation and React rendering after notification.
method.correlation: One outstanding pull on an otherwise idle config sync channel. Every reply must match the entire expected config; any extra config reference update outside a request aborts the block. The production protocol does not echo a pull request ID.
method.payload: Repeating 64-character ASCII pattern; not a binary image, encrypted wire size or a raw carrier throughput test. Decoded full-config byte lengths include normal config fields and two synthetic fields.
method.quantile: Zero-based sorted index floor(n*p), capped at n-1. No outlier removal or forced GC. All failures retained; publication requires a complete, failure-free run.
method.blockMean: Elapsed time for 20 consecutive calls divided by 20; includes full-content validation and loop overhead, unlike the individual notification latency.
method.inference: One Windows host/session, six order-balanced rounds per size and mode; descriptive statistics, no confidence interval or universal speedup claim. Endpoints differ from the small status-command benchmark.

backendSourceVerification.comparison: Runtime bytes match the measured hashes; UTF-8 sources match Git objects after CRLF/LF normalization.
